page: Microsoft Azure F32-16ams_v7 is an AMD-based virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a single thread per core, the system eliminates hyperthreading contention while supplying 256.0 GB of system memory, which establishes an elevated ratio of 16.0 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, accompanied by cryptographic support via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, does not include local disk storage, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core compute capabilities, led by a stress-ng single-core score of 3781.78 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 41.02 GB/sec. CPU-based machine learning inference on small models reaches top-tier throughput at 440.91 tokens per second for text generation. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core (60072.05) and PassMark CPU (45285.42) place within the median 50%, bound by the 16-core physical configuration. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 105.68 GB/sec with write throughput at 68.65 GB/sec, contributing to a strong PassMark memory rating of 2852.94.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the provision of high memory capacity alongside high single-core frequency instead of massive parallel core counts. Because local storage is absent, workloads depend entirely on external or networked block storage for persistence. Qualitative resource efficiency favors memory-dense, single-thread-critical environments over highly parallel batch processing. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, caching tiers, data compression pipelines, ETL staging, and low-concurrency scientific computing.
description: Microsoft Azure F32-16ams_v7 is a memory-dense, compute-oriented instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated x86_64 physical cores (one thread per core) and 256.0 GB of RAM, it delivers an expansive 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Architectural features include 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AVX-512 (VNNI, BF16), and advanced cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote volumes for persistence. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core execution speed and compression throughput, balanced by median multi-threaded scores consistent with its 16-core configuration. Its memory subsystem achieves strong PassMark evaluation scores and 105.68 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. F32-16ams_v7 is tailored for memory-heavy databases, in-memory caching layers, compression tasks, and workloads requiring dedicated single-threaded compute coupled with substantial memory capacity.
